object_description: rectangular workshop and trapezoidal forum linked below terrain
design_condition: The rectangular workshop is embedded along the slope edge and reserved in relation to the existing main building, while the trapezoidal forum forms a public center beside largely intact green space and new viewing areas.

positive.statement: The workshop is successfully embedded in the edge of the slope, with a restrained delivery solution.
The idea of expanding the open space to create a second viewing point is convincing.
The spacious eastern green area, fruit-tree theme, path extensions, and informal play areas are appropriately retained or developed.
The generous access axis, guided by zenithal daylight, promises a high-quality meeting place that supports identification with the technical school while respecting the existing main building.
The well-sized training and workshop rooms are well lit through atriums.
The typology of the workshop building fits the town crown and is developed from its context.

negative.statement: The forum's form and size occupy the open space so extensively that the intended public center is only partially recognizable.
The generous paved piazza seems somewhat artificial, and its necessity and significance are doubted.
There is no understandable connection from the piazza to the existing technical center, and the historical context is treated only rudimentarily.
The planting concept remains too reserved to strengthen the integration of the buildings into the surroundings.
Additional corridors to the classrooms compete strongly with the central axis.
The column-free forum has no reference to the sports hall below and therefore raises questions about the supporting structure.
The uses are mostly functional but not optimally organized, and the space for the flow of goods is too limited.
The city-facing facade appears artificial, while the interaction between the two facade languages appears arbitrary.
The overall effect of the project is therefore not convincing.
